summary: M.S. Computer Engineering (May 2026) from RIT with hands-on experience building real-time embedded C++ systems for robotics and administering the Ubuntu Linux infrastructure they run on (NVIDIA Jetson). Deployed and managed a systemd-based service (auto-restart, non-root isolation, static IP networking, remote XRDP administration) alongside distributed pick-and-place robotics, FreeRTOS firmware, and factory-automation control (ABB RobotStudio, TCP sockets).

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Designed wearable gesture-recognition glove: ADXL345 accelerometers (3-DoF) interfaced via I2C to Raspberry Pi with HC-05 Bluetooth; implemented tap-detection algorithm with sensor calibration for real-time HID cursor control.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led 25-member robotics team in national competitions; owned mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and systems integration. Designed custom PCBs in EAGLE; implemented UART/I2C sensor communication with closed-loop microcontroller feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone
bullets: Distributed real-time system: Flutter client → Flask-SocketIO edge server → Jetson+Arduino controller via WebSocket on a statically addressed network. TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup) and dual ToF sensors for visual servoing; 100% pick reliability, 11.5s end-to-end latency.

Deployed the Jetson controller as a systemd service (auto-restart, non-root isolation, env-file config) with XRDP for remote administration; implemented FreeRTOS firmware (32KB Flash/8KB RAM) with 2-link inverse kinematics.

projects.name: ABB RobotStudio Automation Simulation
bullets: Simulated ABB RobotStudio workcell for factory automation press-to-packing pipeline; programmed in RAPID with TCP socket-based pose acquisition and interrupt-driven logic.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: YOLOv8 detection on Jetson → STM32 servo control via UART; FreeRTOS multitasking with shared-memory mutexes, VL53L0X ToF sensing.

awards: Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition, 45 universities (2022)
